reviews.title: Well worth it
reviews.text: This app is the perfect fitness companion! Whether it’s stretching and cooling down, an easy workout or an intense one, this app has you covered. The accountability is built right in. I have easily made this a part of my fitness routine, it’s probably the best app I’ve ever used.

reviews.title: Love the workouts
reviews.text:
I love these workouts. The coach and god workouts are both great. Coupled with eating better, and I’m getting real results that I’m genuinely so excited about and proud of. I look and feel like an athlete again. 

The one thing that I really wish could be improved, though, is integration with Apple Watch. I appreciate that it does connect, but the connection is very spotty and seems to require the screen to stay on. If there was something else I’d like to be improved too is the way it logs the Fitness activity.  It would be great to set the effort from Freeletics as I’m finishing the workout too. 

But really, the app and concept is great and really works. I highly recommend it, especially if you feel like you’re plateauing in fitness.

reviews.title: La mejor app de entrenamiento que he probado
reviews.text: He probado varias aplicaciones de entrenamiento y, hasta ahora, Freeletics es la que más me gusta. Me encanta la variedad de movimientos, la forma en que combina los ejercicios y cómo estructura los workouts. No se siente repetitiva y cada entrenamiento se siente dinámico y bien pensado. También me gusta mucho que incluya movilidad y estiramientos, porque hace que la experiencia sea más completa. La variedad de ejercicios y la manera en que los mezcla hacen que siempre tenga ganas de entrenar. Excelente aplicación.

reviews.title: A Cash Grab with a Predatory Cancellation Process
reviews.text:
Save your money. There are far better workout programs available for free (look up Jeff Nippard) that don’t trap you in a subscription cycle. Freeletics makes it incredibly difficult to unsubscribe. 

Even after I went through the steps to cancel, they auto-renewed my subscription for a second year. When I reached out to customer service to explain the error, they didn't care and flat-out refused a refund. Unless you want to be stuck fighting a constant battle to cancel your plan, avoid this app at all costs.

reviews.title: Love it, but still needs improvement.
reviews.text: I have been using Freeletics for 5 years now, ever since Fitbit cancelled their Coach program, which was another blind decision by Google. But, I found Freeletics to be better in multiple ways, especially treating you and pushing you like a real athlete. I am 64 years old, and I need to be pushed. Freeletics falls down in the specific exercises where it does not tell or show you which muscles each exercise will stretch or work. It shows a general view of the muscles for a circuit, but it should show that information on individual exercises (when you click on them for instructions) and describe the pull or push of the individual muscles you are working during the specific exercise. That would be more helpful like a coach, rather than a simple timer.  Less important, I want to stop being asked the same thing each day and prefer to turn off all the questions about sharing the workout and results.

reviews.title: Bang for buck
reviews.text: Used to be an elite lifter, but been out of gym for 6 years due to a back injury. Forward to 2026, wasn’t able to do more than 2 pushups in January. I been using the everyday strength plan for 3 days a week and i am at 10+ strict form archer push up in just 3 months. The adapting workouts really helped. When i gave feedback on push ups being hard, it curated routines that focused on bullet proofing my shoulders and posterior chain & core. Overall i feel great, and every time i follow these routines they feel  very satisfying.

reviews.title: Groundhog Day
reviews.text:
I’ve been consistently using this app and, unfortunately, it hasn’t lived up to expectations. The workouts feel very repetitive, often cycling through the exact same exercises for multiple rounds — sometimes up to ten — which makes it hard to stay engaged or feel challenged.

Another issue is the lack of balance in the programming. The stretching routines don’t always align with the muscles being worked. I’ve noticed time spent stretching areas that weren’t used, while the muscles that were actually targeted are sometimes overlooked. This makes the recovery portion feel ineffective.

Most importantly, I haven’t seen any meaningful results, including weight loss, despite sticking with the program. The combination of repetitive workouts, mismatched stretching, and lack of progress has made the experience frustrating overall.

I was hoping for a more dynamic, well-rounded fitness program that adapts and delivers results, but this app hasn’t provided that.

reviews.title: Could be great but developers don’t respond to user frustrations
reviews.text:
I’ve been using Freeletics for a while, and while the AI-driven workouts are promising, there’s a big drawback: you can’t really customize or give feedback on certain parts of the routine. The warm-ups are often too intense with no way to dial them down, and the cooldowns only give you a fixed 5-second transition between exercises, which is often just not enough time. You end up fumbling with the phone to find a workaround, which breaks the flow.

Worse, the support forums are full of users asking for these features, but the developers aren’t listening. If they do respond they just say you’re on the wrong Journey (long-term workout plan), even though it’s the same issue across all Journeys. The app could be really great, but until they let users actually tweak these things or listen to feedback, it’s not worth the subscription cost. When my subscription runs out I’m switching to BodBot which is also not great, extremely clunky app, but at least it’s actually adaptable.

reviews.title: Great app, but lacking basic features
reviews.text:
Every exercise automatically pauses music playing on Spotify. Every time the app switches to a new exercise or set, it pauses my music. 

You can’t post your workouts easily to the community tab. I have to press the button repeatedly to share like 15 times, and then sometimes it uploads it without my photo.

I’ve reached out to the support team before about this, but it’s been years and they still don’t have a feature to share your workout to other apps and include a photo. Instead, the workout is just a vague list of the titles of each segment of your workout with random statistics about the workout. There’s no useful information that shows what you’ve accomplished and you can’t even personalize the post with your own photo. It’s just a generic blue background that, frankly, looks ugly. 

The app routinely crashes as well if you switch to another app like a music player or instagram while waiting in between sets.

reviews.title: Good, not AI Driven
reviews.text:
I’ve used this app quite a bit, on and off, over the last three years or so. When I started with the 15-min session, I found that my overall physicality and flexibility were much improved. I only like this apps body workouts as the weighted plans are a bit jank (in my opinion).

Freeletics does have some UI issues. It’s wayyy harder than it needs to be when generating custom workouts. 

However, my biggest complaint has to do with the “AI”. Pretty sure it’s just an algorithm. For instance, I went from the 15-min to a more comprehensive plan over 6-9 months, then stopped working out for a long time. When I jumped back into the app, expecting the workouts to dial themselves back, instead I was expected to do the reps my former body could accomplish…. It took several weeks of me tuning the workouts to get it back to a reasonable level.

All said and done, great app for guided workouts that take physical flexibility into account. Not a great UI nor AI.
